ios.desc:
The pocket sprite editor for PICO-8. Copy a sprite on your Mac, edit it on your iPhone, paste it straight back.

Pixel Edit Lite is a small, touch-first pixel art and sprite editor for iPhone. Draw with your finger, work offline, and create retro sprites whenever inspiration strikes.

Work on a single sprite or build out a full sprite sheet — navigate between sprites, duplicate them, and copy and paste between sprites. Choose 8×8, 16×16, 32×32, or 64×64 canvases for sprites, game art, icons, and other pixel art projects. Built with PICO-8 and TIC-80 style sprite workflows in mind, with real PICO-8 clipboard format support: copy a sprite in PICO-8 on your Mac, paste it here, edit, and paste it back.

Features

• Clean, minimal interface
• Always-on sprite sheet with navigation, duplication, and copy/paste
• 8×8, 16×16, 32×32, and 64×64 canvases
• Precision pixel drawing with pencil, eraser, and fill
• Shape tools: line, rectangle, and circle, outlined or filled
• Undo and redo
• PICO-8 and TIC-80 color palettes
• Grid-based editing
• Rotate, flip, and shift tools
• Fast, responsive touch controls
• Automatic local saving
• Recent Projects — reopen past sheets in one tap
• Import and export through Files, including iCloud Drive
• Share via the native Share Sheet — AirDrop, Messages, save to Photos, and more
• Real PICO-8 sprite clipboard format support
• Works offline

Pixel Edit Lite is intentionally simple. No complicated desktop-style workflow — just a small pixel editor you can keep with you when you're away from your computer.

quotes.text:
I made a tiny iPhone sprite editor during Covid, when I was pretty obsessed with PICO-8 and wanted to draw sprites even when I was away from my Mac.

I shipped it in 2023, then neglected it for a few years. I’m getting back into it now, fixing things as I find them and adding small features suggested by PICO-8 users.

The original idea was simple: copy a sprite from PICO-8 on the Mac, paste it on your phone, tweak a few pixels, and paste it back. It uses PICO-8’s native clipboard format. It’s a one time $2.99 purchase, with no account or subscription, and works offline.

I’m now considering:

A) Frame by frame animation using sprite sheet regions
B) Opening .p8 carts directly and editing sprites in place

For PICO-8 users, which would you actually use?

I got introduced to pico8 during Covid and absolutely loved it. It piqued interest in me to create sprites and that led me to create a very basic minimalistic sprite editor for pico8.

I first published the app a few years ago in 2023 and lately updated it in the past few months. I am planning to add animation next but still struggling with to keep the UI as simple and minimalistic.

Here is the App Store Link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pixel-edit-lite/id1665723146

quotes.text:
Create pixel art for TIC-80 & PICO-8 fantasy consoles with ease using our minimalistic 16X16 canvas sprite editor for iOS.

I stumbled upon pico8 in HN sometime in 2020[1], and loved the simplicity and constraints of it. I wanted to create pico8 sprites on the go, while away from my MBP. This iOS app is an attempt at making it mobile while keeping the drawing tools simple and comes with 3 palettes (pico8, pico8 secret & tic80)

I would love for you guys to give it a try and happy to get feedback and feature requests for the next iteration of the app.

[1] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=22342295
